units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And we are at the sandwich.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You're at the corner of Orleans and Erie.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Mr. Beef opened in 1979 as a stand, founded by Joe Zucchero, and his family still runs it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the story is that it's the Bear restaurant.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It inspired the television show The Bear, and its storefront is the one in the show.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One account says the sales went up from about three hundred sandwiches a day to more than eight hundred.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll go along with the crowd. Tell me about Italian beef.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It starts in the early twentieth century.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Italian immigrant families were often sold cheaper, tougher cuts of meat, like the roast or the ends of the cow.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And they made it work.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They cooked it for a long time to tenderize it, sliced it very thin to stretch the supply, and served it on fresh bread.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was common at wedding gatherings.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Historians largely believe a shop called Al's was the first to sell it, starting in the 1930s.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So a sandwich that comes from making do.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a hard-times sandwich, yes.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Thin beef, sweet peppers or the pickled vegetable relish called giardiniera, in an Italian loaf, with the meat's juices on top.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What's the order?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One Chicago historian orders his lightly dipped, to avoid soggy bread, with both hot and mild peppers and a little mustard.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's his order, not a rule.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Light dip. Hot and mild. I'm remembering that.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The menu also has hamburgers, hot dogs, fries and pizza puffs.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the restaurant has been on television, including on The Tonight Show.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So I order, I eat, I stand in line.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In that order, probably the other way around.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll bet you a dollar I get beef on my sleeve.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: I'll take that bet.
